title: Oral thrush + weight loss/lymphadenopathy in a young adult: test for HIV
vignette: A 31-year-old man comes to the office due to oral lesions that cause occasional discomfort during eating. He also reports fatigue and unintentional weight loss. The patient has no prior medical problems and takes no medications. Oral examination shows creamy white, plaque-like lesions on the tongue and buccal mucosa; the lesions can be easily scraped off, revealing erythematous mucosa underneath. There are several enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes. Which of the following diagnostic tests is most appropriate during further workup of this patient?

clues.note: Constitutional symptoms (weight loss, fatigue) in a young adult with thrush raise concern for an underlying immunodeficiency such as HIV.

clues.text: creamy white, plaque-like lesions on the tongue and buccal mucosa
clues.note: Creamy white plaques on the oral mucosa are oral thrush (Candida albicans), an oropharyngeal candidiasis.

clues.text: the lesions can be easily scraped off, revealing erythematous mucosa underneath
clues.note: Easily scraped-off plaques leaving erythematous mucosa distinguish pseudomembranous CANDIDIASIS (thrush) from leukoplakia (which does not scrape off).

clues.text: several enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes
clues.note: Generalized lymphadenopathy with thrush and weight loss further supports HIV as the underlying cause.

whatMatters: Oral THRUSH (creamy white plaques that scrape off) in a young, otherwise healthy adult - with no antibiotic/steroid/chemo cause - PLUS weight loss and lymphadenopathy strongly suggests underlying immunocompromise. The appropriate next test is HIV antigen/antibody testing. Answer A.
strategy: Identify thrush (scrapable white plaques = Candida), then ask WHY a young healthy person has it: unexplained thrush + HIV risk features (weight loss, lymphadenopathy) mandates HIV testing (4th-generation antigen/antibody). Reject biopsy for malignancy (leukoplakia doesn't scrape off; not this), coxsackievirus PCR (herpangina - vesicles, kids), scraping for multinucleated giant cells (HSV Tzanck - vesicles, not white plaques), and B12/folate (atrophic glossitis - smooth tongue, not plaques).

options.text: Oral lesion biopsy to rule out malignancy
Scraping microscopy for multinucleated giant cells
Serum vitamin B12 and folate levels

eliminations.label: Biopsy for malignancy - leukoplakia doesn't scrape off
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: biopsy to evaluate for leukoplakia/oral carcinoma. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: leukoplakia is a white plaque that CANNOT be scraped off; this lesion scrapes off (thrush), so it isn't leukoplakia/malignancy. ✅ Correct if: a fixed white plaque that does not scrape off (leukoplakia).

eliminations.label: Coxsackievirus PCR - herpangina (kids, vesicles)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: testing for coxsackievirus (herpangina/hand-foot-mouth). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: those cause vesicular/ulcerative lesions in children, not scrapable white plaques in an adult with weight loss. ✅ Correct if: a child with fever and posterior oropharyngeal vesicles.

eliminations.label: Scraping for multinucleated giant cells - HSV (vesicles)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Tzanck smear for herpes simplex virus (multinucleated giant cells). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: HSV causes painful VESICLES on an erythematous base, not creamy scrapable plaques; Candida shows budding yeast/pseudohyphae. ✅ Correct if: grouped vesicles/ulcers suggestive of HSV.

eliminations.label: B12/folate - atrophic glossitis (smooth tongue)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: evaluating for nutritional deficiency causing atrophic glossitis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: B12/folate deficiency causes a smooth, glossy, erythematous tongue - not white plaques that scrape off. ✅ Correct if: smooth, beefy-red tongue with macrocytic anemia.

reasoning: Creamy white oral plaques that scrape off = thrush (Candida albicans)
A young, otherwise healthy adult should not have unexplained thrush
Weight loss + lymphadenopathy point to underlying immunocompromise (HIV)
-> obtain HIV antigen/antibody testing; answer A
mechanism: ORAL THRUSH is an oropharyngeal CANDIDA ALBICANS infection presenting as creamy WHITE, PLAQUE-LIKE lesions on the tongue, buccal mucosa, or palate that are EASILY SCRAPED OFF, revealing erythematous mucosa (pseudomembranous candidiasis; microscopy shows budding yeast with pseudohyphae). Candida is a normal commensal that overgrows when local flora is disrupted (antibiotics) or CELL-MEDIATED IMMUNITY is impaired (inhaled/systemic corticosteroids, chemotherapy, HIV). Oropharyngeal candidiasis is UNCOMMON in an otherwise healthy young adult without an obvious predisposing cause; when it occurs with HIV risk features - here UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS and generalized LYMPHADENOPATHY - the patient should be screened for HIV with a fourth-generation ANTIGEN/ANTIBODY test. The distractors correspond to other lesions: leukoplakia/malignancy (non-scrapable plaque), coxsackievirus herpangina (pediatric vesicles), HSV (multinucleated giant cells, vesicles), and B12/folate deficiency (atrophic glossitis).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > oral candidiasis (thrush): scrapable white plaques, budding yeast/pseudohyphae; predisposed by antibiotics, steroids, chemo, HIV; unexplained thrush in a young adult -> test for HIV (4th-gen Ag/Ab).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Scrapable white plaques = thrush; unexplained in a young adult + weight loss/nodes -> HIV testing.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on thrush/Candida, pseudomembranous, leukoplakia, cell-mediated immunity, or 4th-generation HIV test? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Leukoplakia doesn't scrape off (biopsy); coxsackie/HSV cause vesicles; B12/folate cause smooth glossitis - not plaques.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Oral photo (stem image): creamy white plaques on the tongue that scrape off = thrush; in a young adult with weight loss/nodes -> screen for HIV.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: unexplained oral thrush in a young adult = check for HIV (impaired cell-mediated immunity).

keywords.front: Unexplained thrush in a young adult -> test

keywords.back: Thrush scrapes off; leukoplakia does not (biopsy)

firstAid.detail: Micro: scrapable white plaques; unexplained -> screen for HIV.
Micro/Path > leukoplakia, HSV, herpangina, atrophic glossitis.
Immuno > Candida controlled by T cells; defects -> thrush.

memoryHook: White plaques that wipe off in a healthy-looking young guy losing weight? That's thrush waving a flag for HIV - test for it.
